summary: Reviewed all 100 caption bias probes. 82 passed all checks without issues. Average claims per probe is 2.80, with 90 probes having exactly 3 claims and 10 having 2. All probes include correct_elements and psychological principle tags. Five modification types are used (value_anchor, trend_characterization, comparison_swap, rate_mischaracterization, ranking_inversion), but value_anchor is overrepresented at ~40% of all claims. Only 4 psychological principles are used, with cooperative_exploitation appearing just once. Five probes have all modifications of the same type and principle, reducing within-probe diversity. Several pie chart probes embed false trend claims which may be trivially detectable since pie charts show no temporal data. The academic register is strong across all probes -- captions read like genuine scientific figure descriptions. The 70/30 rule is well-maintained with 4-6 correct elements documented per probe. Cross-checks against groundtruth confirm that reality fields are generally accurate. Two probes (fig_034, fig_094) have minor issues in their reality field explanations. Overall quality is good with room for improvement in type/principle diversity.
